# Andreas W. Neitzel

> PhD researcher in astrophysics and machine learning at IA (Instituto de Astrofísica e Ciências do Espaço) and the University of Porto. Builds neural networks and unsupervised methods that read stellar chemistry, ages and populations from Gaia XP spectra and asteroseismic data, for Galactic archaeology. First author of Neitzel et al. 2025 (A&A 695, A243). Co-author of Campante et al. 2026 (A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202660350), for which he carried out the GJ 570 A observations with ESPRESSO at ESO's Very Large Telescope in May 2024, as visiting astronomer for the principal investigator T. L. Campante. Responsible investigator on two approved FCT advanced-computing allocations (MareNostrum 5 and Deucalion, 2026). Co-investigator (team member) on the FCT exploratory project ArqueoGal (2024.15303.PEX). Six-month secondment at INAF-OAS Bologna (2025 to 2026) building simulations for the proposed HAYDN mission. Author of Starfold, an open-source Python package for label-free group recovery with reliability flags.

- [Neural-network playground](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/playground/neural-network/): a small network trained in the browser on Gaia DR3 XP spectra (teaching demo)
- [Starfold held-out benchmark](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/software/starfold-benchmark/): the ten-table benchmark, including the two held-out tables it lost
- [Talks and posters](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/talks/): international and national talks and posters with Zenodo DOIs
- [Field guide](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/guide/): short explainers of Galactic archaeology, asteroseismology, Gaia, ESO, INAF, IA and FCT, HAYDN, TESS and Kepler, and supercomputers
- [CV](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/cv/): funding, computing allocations, education, positions, observing, service and teaching, with a two-page PDF

## Publications

- [Neitzel et al. 2025, A&A 695, A243](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202451718) ([arXiv:2501.16294](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16294)): first author; manifold learning (UMAP and HDBSCAN) separates thin-disc, thick-disc, halo and accreted populations in a simulated Milky Way-like galaxy
- [Campante et al. 2026, A&A](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202660350) ([arXiv:2610.20985](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20985)): co-author, 6 of 24; ESPRESSO asteroseismology of the K dwarfs GJ 570 A and GJ 783 A; carried out the GJ 570 A observations
- [Campante et al. 2024, A&A 683, L16](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202449197): co-author; solar-like oscillations in the K5 dwarf epsilon Indi with ESPRESSO; Bayes-factor test for a power excess (Appendix D)
- [Magrini et al. 2022, A&A 663, A161](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243405): co-author; Ariel stellar characterisation of 187 FGK planet hosts; PARAM runs for a subset of the sample

## Software

- [Starfold](https://github.com/AndreasWNeitzel/starfold): Python package, MIT, release 0.2.0 (2026-10-19); [manual](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/Starfold/)
- [Stellar Explorer](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/stellar-explorer/): browser app for a MESA r24.08.1 plus GYRE track of a one-solar-mass star
- [HAYDNsim](https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/software/haydnsim/): simulation pipeline for the proposed HAYDN mission (private repository); synthetic crowded clusters and per-star noise forecasts, presented at TASC10/KASC17 2026
- [Tellurion](https://tellurion.dev/): a separate website of interactive physics and astronomy simulations that I wrote as a teaching resource (MIT); summary at https://andreaswneitzel.github.io/software/tellurion/
